title: Language bindings: patterns for streaming + tool-call + typed outputs
creator: Priya Raman
description: Produce a set of concrete, language-specific binding patterns and examples that demonstrate: 1) streaming responses with incremental structured payloads, 2) function/tool calling handshake semantics across TypeScript/Python/Go SDKs, and 3) compatibility shims so older clients can interoperate with new structured envelopes. Deliverables are: RFC-style pattern doc + short runnable examples for each language + migration notes for customers.
background: Recent runtime changes introduce an event-envelope streaming format that sends partial structured records (typed chunks) alongside free-form text. Some customers use older SDKs that expect raw text chunks; others require strongly typed outputs for downstream parsers and tool-invocation. We must supply idiomatic binding patterns and a minimal compatibility shim so teams can upgrade server-side without breaking clients.
spec: High-level spec to implement in examples: 1) Stream event envelope shape: {event_type, seq, payload, schema_id, signature?}. 2) Tool-call handshake: client sends request with `tools` descriptor; runtime emits `tool_request` envelope when model decides to call; SDK should surface a typed callback and await `tool_result` or provide a helper to auto-execute registered handlers. 3) Partial structured outputs: payloads may represent partial JSON trees; SDK converges them into final typed object using a deterministic merge and validates against provided JSON Schema or protobuf descriptor. 4) Backpressure: provide a simple flow-control API in TS/Py/Go so consumers can pause/resume stream processing when downstream is overloaded.
acceptance_criteria: Pattern doc published in the SDK repo docs folder covering all three languages
Three runnable example apps (one TS, one Python, one Go) demonstrating: streaming structured envelopes, a tool-call lifecycle, and graceful compatibility with legacy text-stream clients
Compatibility shim packaged as a small module in each language that converts new event envelopes to legacy text frames and vice versa
Integration tests: simulate mixed-version clients and show no regression in latency or error surface for hosted customers
Code reviewed and merged with at least two engineering approvals and docs review by Developer Experience
implementation_notes: Split work into two sub-tasks: A) Reference implementation + examples, B) Lightweight compatibility shim and integration tests. Keep examples minimal but idiomatic: TypeScript should use async iterators and event emitters; Python should use async generators + Pydantic model validation; Go should expose a channel-based iterator and typed struct builder. Avoid heavy deps; prefer small libs (pydantic-core/cattrs, protobuf-lite) and add feature flags so customers opt-in. Note: maintain binary compatibility for on-prem packaging.
migration_notes: For customers on older SDKs: 1) Enable a compatibility flag on the server (`legacy_text_frames: true`) to continue sending legacy text frames alongside envelopes. 2) Provide guidance to migrate in three steps: run shim in pass-through mode, enable typed envelope parsing in staging, turn on tool-call handlers with canary traffic. Document sample runtime config and expected traffic patterns.
risks: Potential customer confusion if runtime flips to envelope-only mode without a wide-available shim. Testing surface increases due to combinatorial permutations of client versions and runtime feature flags.
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope parser in each language, e2e test that runs example client against local runtime test harness that emits: text frames only, envelopes only, and mixed. Latency regression benchmark to ensure shim adds <3% p50 on streaming throughput. Add a chaos job that injects partial payload reorderings to validate merge logic.
